summary: Release→import and content/search largely reuse startImport’s generation guard, consumeControl, and reset/abort lifecycle, matching startBuildJob. The main divergence is that release now starts async work but still skips the sibling respondUnlessDropped / dropNextResponse arm used by every other work-starting submission.

findings.summary: Release now starts an import but still answers with bare sendStatus instead of respondUnlessDropped.
findings.rationale: Sibling work-starting submissions — builder PUT, DM upload (may queue build), DM `/build`, and Pinpoint package upload — all call respondUnlessDropped after recording work so dropNextResponse models accepted-but-response-lost. Release previously only flipped isReleased (and was omitted from the FakeControls dropNextResponse docstring). It now calls startReleaseDrivenImport (same async family as startImport/startBuildJob) then sendStatus(res, 200) directly, so the one-shot drop arm cannot cover this new submission even though DM verify retries release when isReleased is false.

findings.summary: Missing publication.parentId silently no-ops release-driven import after isReleased is already set.
findings.rationale: startReleaseDrivenImport returns without starting work when parentId is undefined. The call site in handleDataManager has already set revision.isReleased = true, so the HTTP release succeeds with no import record. Direct /import/pinpointPackage fails closed with ERR6003 when neither importInformation.json nor query ids yield a target. Publications may be created without parentId; the new release→import path has no equivalent refused/absent arm and leaves a released revision that combined observe/verify cannot satisfy.

findings.summary: Unreadable package bytes become an empty document map and COMPLETED, unlike DM upload’s isZip failure arm.
findings.rationale: documentsFromPackage uses listZipEntries(pkg) ?? [] then startImport marks COMPLETED. DM upload refuses non-zip packages (FAILED) before startBuildJob; builder corruptNextOutput intentionally yields a non-zip that release will still import to COMPLETED with no documents. Import’s only failure one-shot remains failNextImport — there is no corrupt/unreadable-package failure sibling on the new release-driven path, so corrupt build output looks like a successful empty import rather than a failed one.
